title: Exponential bound for polynomial exponents
statement: For all natural numbers $K$ and $k$, there exist natural numbers $A$ and $e$ such that, for every natural number $n$, $2^{K(n+1)^k}\le A(2^n)^e$.
replaced:
For all constants $K, k \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist constants $A, e \in \mathbb{N}$
such that $2^{K (n+1)^k} \le A \cdot 2^{n^e}$ for every $n$.
